text:
Elena: Heads-up: nightly bench shows a p99 spike after we enabled the new kernel routing rule. Opening a triage thread.
bench-bot: nightly-run 1765432099 finished. model=redwood-llama-13b profile=fused-attn routing=policy-v3 p50=12ms p95=78ms p99=243ms throughput=120 tok/s notes=more-fallbacks
Tariq: Can you paste the raw deltas? p99 -> 243ms seems large. Is that for long sequences?
Elena: Confirmed it's driven by tails. Looking at sample stratification, bucket 512+ seqs had p99 jump from 190 -> 430. Full dump in S3: <https://s3.redwood/internal/bench/1765432099/results.json>
Ben: Two quick hypotheses: (1) the routing policy pushed some requests to a fallback kernel with no fused-attn kernel compiled for quantized config, (2) distribution shift -> more long sequences in this run.
Jia: We recently changed the sample corpus to include 20% more chat logs — that will skew seq length. We should use explicit sequence-length bucketing in the harness to avoid sampling noise.
Maia: Also check cuda kernel selection logs on the hosts, fallback reasons are logged: "kernel_select: no matching kernel for q4_bitpack -> fallback=scalar_attn". If we see that across many hosts, it's a binary compat/compile issue.
bench-bot: host-summary: host-12 fallback=scalar_attn count=312 host-7 fallback=fused_attn_v1 count=48 kernel-mix=high
Tariq: Repro plan: (A) run deterministic harness with seed and fixed buckets; (B) run quantization toggle true/false; (C) run single-host microbench to isolate kernel behavior. Who can run (A)?
Elena: I'll run (A) now with deterministic seed + bucket config. Command I'm using:
```
./bench_harness --model redwood-llama-13b \
  --profile fused-attn-routing \
  --samples 5000 \
  --seed 1337 \
  --buckets "[64,128,256,512,1024]" \
  --save results/1765432100-deterministic.json
```
Ben: Add --record-kernel-log to that run so we can correlate samples to kernel choices.
Elena: Good call, re-running with that flag.
Jia: If deterministic run reproduces the p99 gap only in >512 bucket, then it's sampling distribution, not a nondeterministic perf glitch. If it's across buckets, probably a codepath/regression in kernel selector.
Maia: Also sanity-check correctness: compare top-k logits between fused-attn and fallback for a subset to exclude subtle correctness regressions introduced by quantized kernels. Script:
```
python tools/compare_logits.py --base results/golden.json --cand results/1765432100-deterministic.json --threshold 1e-3 --samples 100
```
Tariq: If correctness diffs are nontrivial, escalate to runtime-ml. Otherwise focus on routing policy and kernel compatibility.
bench-bot: ran quick micro-run on host-12: fused_attn_v2 latency_p99=235ms fallback_scalar_attn latency_p99=510ms quant_mode=q4_0
Elena: Deterministic run uploaded. Quick summary: buckets <=256 stable, 512 shows p99=420ms, kernel_log indicates ~65% of 512+ prefixed requests hit fallback due to mismatch in kernel signature (q4 alignment).
Ben: That points to compilation/config mismatch. Did the recent kernel ABI change (padding/alignment) make some q4 kernels opt-out? Check the last deploy PR: https://git.internal/r/ops/3131
Jia: I remember a compile flag was toggled to improve throughput on A100; it changed alignment behavior for q4. We need a compatibility shim in kernel selector that detects ABI and falls back to appropriate compiled kernel variant instead of scalar fallback.
Maia: Short-term mitigation: update routing policy to prefer hosts labeled "legacy-q4-compat" for models with q4 profiles until we can roll a shim. I'll add a temporary policy.
Tariq: Action items: Elena to run expanded microbench across 3 hosts and upload kernel logs (owner: Elena). Ben to draft a small selector shim PR (owner: Ben). Jia to run correctness diff for 200 samples across buckets (owner: Jia). Maia to patch routing policy for next 2 deploys (owner: Maia). ETA EOD tomorrow.
Elena: Noted. Uploading artifacts and linking to ticket INC-2147: <https://redwood.internal/incidents/INC-2147>
Ben: One more ask — we should add an automated assertion in the bench harness: if p99 increases >20% for any bucket vs baseline, fail the nightly run and collect kernel logs automatically. Small PR incoming.
Jia: Agree. Also recommend we store per-bucket baseline percentiles to reduce false positives from sampling noise.
Maia: I'll schedule a short sync tomorrow 11am to review artifacts. Posting calendar invite. :calendar:
Elena: thanks all. Will post final summary in the ticket and close the loop when shim PR lands. :thumbsup:
